user.title: Add purchase
user.description:
Record a Purchase even if no devices have arrived or been added to Home Assistant yet. You can link physical devices now or attach Assets to this Purchase later.

Close the window without saving by using the X button in the upper-left corner.

data_description.device_ids: Leave empty to create the Purchase before any devices exist. If selected, a physical Home Assistant device can belong to only one active Purchase.
data_description.warranty_type: 1 and 2 year warranties are calculated automatically from the purchase date. Use Manual only for another end date.
data_description.purchase_price: Total purchase price, not per-device price. The configured Home Assistant currency is stored with the purchase.
data_description.receipt_url: Optional URL to a receipt, invoice or other purchase document.
data_description.installed_date: For selected devices, leave empty to use the Purchase date as their initial Installation date. You can edit or clear it later.

reconfigure.description:

{linked_assets}

Removing a registry device removes its Lifecycle entity from this Purchase but preserves its Asset and Asset ID. Change a manually managed Asset's Purchase from Manage Asset → Link to Purchase.

user.title: Add runtime tracking
user.description:
First choose the physical device and runtime detection method. Next, select a source entity suitable for that method.

Close the window without saving by using the X button in the upper-left corner.

data_description.device_id: The Runtime hours sensor is linked to this physical Home Assistant device and its persistent Device Lifecycle Asset. Service-type HA devices are rejected.
data_description.runtime_mode: Choose whether runtime is detected from an entity being on or from measured power.

runtime_source.title: Configure runtime source
runtime_source.description:
The source list is filtered for the selected tracking method. Power mode shows only actual power sensors; on-state mode shows sensible on/off entities.

Close the window without saving by using the X button in the upper-left corner.

data_description.source_entity_id: Power mode accepts Power device-class sensors whose unit can be converted to watts. On-state mode accepts switches, lights, binary sensors, input booleans and fans. Device Lifecycle's own entities are excluded.
data_description.power_threshold: Runtime starts when the source power, normalized to watts, rises above this threshold.
data_description.power_hysteresis: Prevents toggling around the threshold. Example: 10 W threshold and 2 W hysteresis starts above 10 W and stops below 8 W. Must be between 0 and the threshold.

stale_primary_device.title: Primary Home Assistant device unavailable: {asset_name} ({asset_id})
stale_primary_device.description:
The primary Home Assistant device of {asset_name} ({asset_id}) is no longer in Home Assistant.

Device Lifecycle kept this relationship on purpose. Nothing has been removed or replaced automatically, and the Asset and its entities are unchanged.

To repair it, open [Device Lifecycle](/config/integrations/integration/device_lifecycle):

1. If a Purchase still lists the device, reconfigure that Purchase and remove the device from its Home Assistant devices.
2. If Runtime tracking still uses the device, delete that Runtime configuration. The Asset keeps its Runtime total.
3. Choose **Configure** → **Manage devices** → {asset_id} → **Home Assistant devices** → **Manage primary Home Assistant device**, then replace or unlink the device.

If the same Home Assistant device returns to Home Assistant, this issue clears by itself.

stale_related_device.title: Related Home Assistant device unavailable: {asset_name} ({asset_id})
stale_related_device.description:
A related Home Assistant device of {asset_name} ({asset_id}) is no longer in Home Assistant.

Device Lifecycle kept this relationship on purpose. Nothing has been removed automatically, and the Asset and its entities are unchanged.

To remove the relationship, open [Device Lifecycle](/config/integrations/integration/device_lifecycle) and choose **Configure** → **Manage devices** → {asset_id} → **Home Assistant devices** → **Remove related Home Assistant device**. The device is listed there as Home Assistant device unavailable.

If the same Home Assistant device returns to Home Assistant, this issue clears by itself.

runtime_archived_asset.title: Runtime tracking conflicts with an archived device: {asset_name} ({asset_id})
runtime_archived_asset.description:
Runtime tracking is still configured for {asset_name} ({asset_id}), but the device is archived. This usually happens after restoring a backup.

Runtime tracking for it is paused. Nothing has been deleted: the device keeps its accumulated Runtime, its Runtime entity and history, and the Runtime configuration is kept unchanged.

To resolve it, open [Device Lifecycle](/config/integrations/integration/device_lifecycle) and either restore the device, or delete this Runtime tracking configuration.

Dismissing this issue does not resolve the conflict.
